p1-v1.alt: The Perseverance rover and the little Ingenuity helicopter travel together through space toward Mars.

textos.texto: July 2020. The Perseverance rover launches toward Mars. It carries a passenger hidden under its belly: the Ingenuity helicopter.
How exciting! We're going to Mars!

p1-v2.alt: Two jars of air: Earth's is full of little balls and Mars's is almost empty. Ingenuity looks at them from below.

textos.texto: Flying on Mars is very hard: its air is about 100 times thinner than Earth's.
There's hardly any air to push!
Earth
Mars

p1-v3.alt: A close-up of Ingenuity: two rotors, one above the other, with arrows showing they spin in opposite directions; a scale stands next to it.

textos.texto: That's why Ingenuity is very light and its two rotors spin in opposite directions, very fast: about 2,400 turns per minute. Much faster than a helicopter on Earth!
1.8 kg

p1-v4.alt: Perseverance, in Jezero Crater, looks at Ingenuity, which is already on the ground.

textos.texto: February 2021. Perseverance lands in Jezero Crater. Weeks later, it carefully sets Ingenuity down on the ground.
You'll be safe here, little one.
Thanks! Now it's my turn.

p2-v1.alt: At night, under a starry sky, Ingenuity shivers next to a thermometer showing it is extremely cold.

textos.texto: Nights on Mars are freezing: as cold as 90 degrees below zero (Celsius). Ingenuity had to use energy to keep warm.
Brrr, so cold!

p2-v2.alt: Ingenuity's rotors spin so fast they look blurry and kick up dust from the ground.

textos.texto: April 19, 2021. The rotors spin faster and faster…
Here I go!

p2-v3.alt: Ingenuity hovers 3 meters above the ground, over its shadow, while Perseverance watches from afar.

textos.texto: It rose 3 meters, hovered for about 30 seconds and landed again! It was the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
It's flying!
3 m

p2-v4.alt: A photo of Ingenuity's shadow on the Martian ground, and Earth celebrating with one arm raised.

textos.texto: Ingenuity even took a photo of its own shadow on the Martian ground.
Ingenuity is flying! We did it!

p3-v1.alt: Ingenuity flies over hills and rocks; below, Perseverance follows a dotted path.

textos.texto: Ingenuity kept flying and became a scout: from the air, it looked for good routes for Perseverance.
There's a good path this way!

p3-v2.alt: A bar chart: a very short bar for the 5 planned flights and a very tall one for the 72 flights completed.

textos.texto: It was supposed to make only 5 test flights. It made 72 in almost three years!
5 planned
72 flights!

p3-v3.alt: A tired-looking Ingenuity next to a broken piece of one of its blades lying on the ground.

textos.texto: January 2024. On its 72nd flight, one of its blades was damaged. It could not fly anymore.
I don't think I can fly anymore…

p3-v4.alt: At sunset, with a bluish Sun, Ingenuity rests on Mars; outlines of future helicopters appear in the sky.

textos.texto: Ingenuity stayed on Mars. It proved that flying on another planet is possible and opened the way for new helicopter explorers.
Goodbye, Mars! Mission accomplished!

cierre.datoReal: Over its 72 flights, Ingenuity flew for more than 2 hours in total and traveled about 17 kilometers.
cierre.preguntaAula: If you had to design a helicopter for another planet, what would you change depending on its air?
